figures.alt: BERT pretraining predicts masked tokens and sentence relationships; separate downstream models reuse its encoder with classification, token labeling or answer span heads.
figures.caption: BERT pretraining and task adaptation. Reproduced from Devlin et al., Figure 1, NAACL 2019; figure crop, CC BY 4.0.
figures.purpose: The dotted arrows in Figure 1 transfer pretrained parameters, not predictions. The downstream panels share the encoder design but attach different task heads; fine tuning updates the encoder as well as the selected head.

figures.alt: At every packed WordPiece position, BERT adds token, sentence segment and learned absolute position embeddings. Both boundary tokens also receive these embeddings.
figures.caption: Three embeddings form each input vector. Reproduced from Devlin et al., Figure 2, NAACL 2019; figure crop, CC BY 4.0.
figures.purpose: Figure 2 shows addition, not concatenation. Segment A and B identify the two packed spans, while position indices continue across their separator; both spans still inhabit one sequence.
